facts.fact: 她问头去哪儿

facts.fact: Harrison：便宜卖给做标本的商贩再卖给游客；爪一样；尽量不浪费
facts.anchor: We sell them on the cheap to a few vendors who preserve them and sell them to tourists. Same for the claws. We try to limit waste

facts.fact: 她想：总算有一件好事
facts.anchor: Well, that was one good thing

facts.fact: Harrison 不等她回答就宣布讲课结束
facts.anchor: Without waiting for my reply, he said, “Good. Lecture over.

facts.fact: 她判：他显然想赶紧把这事了结
facts.anchor: He clearly wanted to get this done with

facts.fact: 他从附近台面托盘取一把木柄磨损的刀，刃比她预期的短
facts.anchor: he grabbed a knife with a worn wood handle, its blade shorter than I’d expected

facts.fact: 像普通牛排刀但更厚
facts.anchor: Like a normal steak knife but thicker

facts.fact: 剥法有多种，他要示范农场的标准
facts.anchor: We could skin the alligators multiple ways, he explained, but he was going to show me the farm’s standard

facts.fact: 从颈部起、在 scutes（骨板）上方、身体顶端下刀，再沿腿切
facts.anchor: We’d start around the neck, above the scutes—the bony plates—at the top of its body. Then we’d cut along the legs

facts.fact: 他无疑以为她已被新信息冲垮，就停在这里说开始
facts.anchor: No doubt expecting me to be overwhelmed by the onslaught of new information, he stopped there

facts.fact: 他稳了口气，把刀从颈右侧推进鳄鱼背部、连拽三下到另一侧
facts.anchor: he pushed the knife into the alligator’s back to the right of its neck, jerking it three times until it reached the other side

facts.fact: 拔刀时血从刀尖滴到桌上
facts.anchor: blood dripping from its tip onto the table

facts.fact: 他让她沿背部纵向切
facts.anchor: Now you cut along the back. Lengthwise

facts.fact: 她接过刀、贴在他停下的颈部位置；感觉像把勺子按在木桌上
facts.anchor: It was like holding a spoon to a wood table

facts.fact: 她问怎么进得去
facts.anchor: How does it go in?

facts.fact: Harrison 说用锋利那面；他想刻薄但不断咽口水毁了效果
facts.anchor: He was going for snide, but his constant swallowing ruined the effect

facts.fact: 她说那边有垃圾桶，需要就用
facts.anchor: There’s a trash can over there if you need it

facts.fact: 他今早第二次哼，越过桌子把手悬在她手上方问介不介意
facts.anchor: Snorting for the second time that morning, he reached over the table, hovering his hands above mine

facts.fact: dryer sheets 的香味飘来，比他 Greer House 房间里那件衬衫浓十倍
facts.anchor: The fragrance of dryer sheets drifted toward me, ten times stronger than the shirt in his room at Greer House

facts.fact: 他不再笑了；眼神在她两只眼睛间来回，是在讨许可
facts.anchor: His eyes flicked back and forth between mine, asking for permission

facts.fact: 她以为他碰她会让她发慌，但拒绝被吓住，点了点头
facts.anchor: I assumed he thought touching me would unnerve me, but I refused to be bullied. I inclined my head

facts.fact: 他的手包住她的手；掌心起茧、粗糙
facts.anchor: His hand engulfed mine. His palms were callused, rough

facts.fact: 她此前没注意过他的唇：干但不裂，大概柔软
facts.anchor: I hadn’t noticed his lips before. Dry but not cracked. Soft, probably

facts.fact: 他眼盯尸身轻轻下压；刀并不像她以为的那样滑入，它有阻力
facts.anchor: The knife didn’t slip in the way I’d assumed. It resisted

facts.fact: 她倾身、由他带手；如布被撕开的一声裂响，刀咬住了
facts.anchor: With a tear, like fabric ripping, the knife found purchase

facts.fact: 兴奋在体内起涟漪；她想像翻书一样摊开这鳄鱼，看清它怎么运转再画下来
facts.anchor: I could unfurl this alligator’s body like a book. See what made it tick, then capture that in a drawing

facts.fact: 里面的肉是白的，她以为会更红；凑近一看，是粉
facts.anchor: Inside, its flesh was white. I’d expected it to be redder. Releasing the knife, I leaned closer—no, it was pink

facts.fact: 脑中闪过 Michelle 躺在她初中混凝土操场上
facts.anchor: My mind flashed to Michelle, lying on my middle school’s concrete playground

facts.fact: Michelle 的血稀如水彩，却浓如油画颜料
facts.anchor: Her blood had been thin, like a watercolor wash, but richly colored, like oil paint

facts.fact: 她从没见过那样的东西；用手指蘸过血洼举近眼前——句子被破折号截断
facts.anchor: I’d grazed the puddle with a finger, lifting it closer to my eyes—

facts.fact: Harrison 说不舒服可以停
facts.anchor: We can stop if you feel sick

facts.fact: 他的声音把她从记忆里拉出，目光重新聚焦在他脸上
facts.anchor: His voice pulled me from the memory, and my eyes refocused on his face

facts.fact: 她自责控制那么久又走神，还是在人前
facts.anchor: I’d done it again, after controlling myself for so long—let my mind wander into dangerous territory. And in front of someone, too

facts.fact: 她自问：他注意到了吗
facts.anchor: Had he noticed?

facts.fact: 她的判读：没有；他那句话在她停顿时更像得意而非关切
facts.anchor: His voice had been more triumphant than concerned at my pause

facts.fact: 他把她的不动归为恶心而非快感；他以为自己赢了她
facts.anchor: he credited my motionlessness to disgust—not pleasure. He thought he’d beat me

facts.fact: 某一刻他把刀拔出、擦净放在尾巴旁的桌上
facts.anchor: At some point, he’d pulled the knife from the alligator’s body, cleaned it, and set it on the table next to the tail

facts.fact: 她说需要一个时刻——不是谎；请他再讲一遍步骤
facts.anchor: I just need a moment,” I said. Not a lie. “Can you go over the steps one more time?

facts.fact: 他照办；他讲时她用 knife 描轮廓
facts.anchor: He obliged. As he spoke, I traced the outline with the knife

facts.fact: 他讲完她深吸一口气，想象石膏糊上脸、把脸刷成无表情
facts.anchor: imagining plaster pouring over my face, rendering it expressionless

facts.fact: Harrison 半句：我们可以告诉 Gazzie 你不想要——
facts.anchor: Seriously, we can tell Gazzie you don’t want—

facts.fact: 但她已经把刀推进去了
facts.anchor: But I was already pushing the knife in

facts.fact: 她沿鳄鱼侧身切到尾根再横切；绕过尾巴时察觉 Harrison 在让开
facts.anchor: As I stepped around the tail to the table’s other side, I sensed Harrison moving out of my way

facts.fact: 手握刀时她觉得自己能干、掌控得住
facts.anchor: With the knife in my hand, I felt competent, in control

facts.fact: 她自问：这不算邪恶吧
facts.anchor: That wasn’t wicked, was it?

facts.fact: 绕过 scutes 切完后她停下、在围裙上擦刀
facts.anchor: Once I’d cut around the scutes, I stopped and wiped the blade on my apron

facts.fact: 抬头时 Harrison 带着某种担忧盯着她
facts.anchor: When I looked up, Harrison was staring at me with something like worry

facts.fact: 她立刻自问：是不是又走神了
facts.anchor: Had I slipped again?

facts.fact: 他说她是天生的；担忧已变成不甘的笑
facts.anchor: His worried expression had morphed into a begrudging smile

facts.fact: 满足扫过她：他承认她确有能耐，是潜在威胁
facts.anchor: He’d realized I was, in fact, capable. A potential threat

facts.fact: 她想：他若觉得她做得好，Gazzie 也许也会
facts.anchor: If he thought I was doing a good job, maybe Gazzie would, too

facts.fact: 随后愧疚落在胃底：Mama 看到她手里握刀会愤怒
facts.anchor: Then guilt settled in the pit of my stomach. Mama would have been furious to see a knife in my hand

facts.fact: 她问下一步
facts.anchor: “What’s next?

facts.fact: Harrison 一边猛扯皮一边讲：再绕手臂和腹部细切，那最软也最值钱
facts.anchor: then carefully cutting around the arms and belly—the softest, most valuable part

facts.fact: 刮掉碎肉、洗净、挂到后间晾干
facts.anchor: before washing it off and hanging it in the back room to dry

facts.fact: 当天晚些另一名队员——很可能是 Joe——腌皮，工序是往皮上抹盐
facts.anchor: another team member, probably Joe, would cure the hide, a process that involved slathering the skin with salt

facts.fact: 那天下午她们剥了六条鳄鱼
facts.anchor: We skinned six alligators that afternoon

facts.fact: 每条内部都不一样：有的多肉，有的多血
facts.anchor: Each one was different on the inside—some meatier than others, some bloodier

facts.fact: 她细看每一条，好留待日后画
facts.anchor: I examined them carefully so I could sketch them later

facts.fact: 快下班时屋顶工出现、查看天花板裂缝；漏已大到下面要放三只桶
facts.anchor: the leak now large enough to need three buckets under it

facts.fact: 她觉得漏水随她每剥一条翻倍，几乎像水在抗议她的参与
facts.anchor: The leak’s size had doubled with each alligator I skinned, almost like the water was protesting my involvement

facts.fact: 屋顶工抱怨保修，承诺带援兵再来，走回卡车
facts.anchor: Grumbling about warranties, the roofer promised to return with reinforcements and marched back to his truck

facts.fact: 到 Harrison 提议收工时，白肉屑糊住她的围裙
facts.anchor: By the time Harrison suggested we pack up, bits of white flesh coated my apron

facts.fact: 血甚至滑进塑料手套里，手指粉得像墨渍
facts.anchor: Blood had even slipped down into my plastic gloves, and pink covered my fingers like ink stains

facts.fact: 冲桌子时她把手上的东西喷掉
facts.anchor: As we hosed down the table, I sprayed off my hands

facts.fact: 她想象自己天天来剥鳄鱼：我做得到吗
facts.anchor: I imagined myself showing up to skin alligators every day. Could I do it?

facts.fact: 确定感射穿她：能；何止——她想
facts.anchor: Certainty shot through me. Yes, I could. More than that—I wanted to

facts.fact: 当晚离开前 Harrison 锁了挂皮晾干的后间
facts.anchor: Harrison locked the back room, where the skins hung to dry

facts.fact: 他用链条绕住两个把手并以上锁连接
facts.anchor: slung a chain around the two handles, connecting them with a padlock

facts.fact: 剥皮室另加一把挂锁
facts.anchor: He secured the skinning room with another padlock

facts.fact: 他瞥了一眼门上的监控摄像头，对自己点头表示满意
facts.anchor: Glancing at the security camera above the door, he nodded to himself, satisfied

facts.fact: 她想起 Nova 与 Gazzie 那回悄声交谈、Gazzie 坚持当着她别说了
facts.anchor: I remembered Nova’s hushed exchange with Gazzie, Gazzie’s insistence that they stop their discussion in front of me

facts.fact: 她随口说 Gazzie 提过上周丢了东西
facts.anchor: Gazzie mentioned things going missing last week

facts.fact: 她希望那句含糊到能骗 Harrison 以为她知情
facts.anchor: hoping the statement was vague enough to fool him into thinking I knew what I was talking about

facts.fact: 她还加了「down on their luck」一类说法
facts.anchor: Folks down on their luck and all that

facts.fact: Harrison 打量她太久，才又拉了一下挂锁
facts.anchor: He studied me for a moment too long before tugging the padlock once more

facts.fact: 他说被偷的是几张皮；时间正是她的第一天
facts.anchor: A few skins were stolen. Your first day, actually

facts.fact: 她问：几张
facts.anchor: “How many?

facts.fact: Harrison 含糊地「Mmm」：没什么可担心
facts.anchor: he said evasively. “Nothing to worry about
